# Open Port Scanner (open-port-tools/port-scanner)

> Fast, cross-platform open port checker and asynchronous IP network scanner for Windows, macOS, and Linux in native Rust (tokio + egui GPU GUI + CLI). Zero dependencies.

## Summary
Open Port Scanner is a modern, ultra-lightweight open-source utility for discovering open TCP ports, scanning entire local subnets in 1 click (`--lan` / `/24` CIDR), inspecting service banners (SSH, HTTP status, Server headers, and titles), and measuring latency in milliseconds. It compiles to standalone ~2–4 MB binaries without Java, Python, or Npcap/WinPcap kernel drivers. It serves as a modern alternative to Angry IP Scanner, Nmap (Zenmap), and Advanced Port Scanner.

## Key Capabilities
- 1-click local network (`LAN /24`) discovery: auto-detects active subnet while filtering loopback (`127.*`), link-local (`169.254.*`), and VPN virtual ranges (`198.18.0.0/15`).
- High-performance asynchronous Rust engine (`tokio`): sweeps hundreds of hosts and thousands of ports in parallel without socket exhaustion.
- Native GPU desktop GUI (`egui` / `eframe`): dark-mode minimal interface with instant table sorting, real-time search filter, and 1-click CSV/JSON export.
- Full scriptable CLI (`clap`): supports `--json`, `--lan`, `-p`, `--profile`, `-t`, `-c`, and `-o report.json|csv|md`.
- Service identification for 120+ standard ports with banner and HTTP title grabbing.
- Pre-built standalone binaries for Windows x64 (`.exe`), macOS Universal (Apple Silicon M1-M4 & Intel), and Linux x64.

## Quick Commands
- Launch GUI: `port-scanner` or `port-scanner --gui`
- 1-Click LAN scan: `port-scanner --lan --profile quick`
- Check specific ports on host: `port-scanner <target> -p 22,80,443,8080`
- Full 1-65535 scan: `port-scanner <target> --profile full`
- Machine-readable JSON output: `port-scanner 192.168.0.1 --profile web --json -q`
